disclosure.title: Brainling needs Accessibility to count your reels

points.lock: Shows the lock screen when you hit your limit
points.never: Never reads your messages, never sends screen content anywhere

body.what: To count Reels, Shorts, TikToks and Spotlight videos, Brainling uses Android’s AccessibilityService API. While you use Instagram, Instagram Lite, YouTube, TikTok, Facebook, Facebook Lite or Snapchat, it reads screen layout information (which screen is open, the names of on-screen elements, and scroll events).
body.use: We use this only to: count how many short videos you watch, show your count and mascot, and — if you set a limit — cover the reels screen or go back when you reach it.
body.never: What we never do: we do not read or store your messages, comments, video titles or what is in the videos. We do not record your screen. Everything is processed on your phone and is not sent to us or anyone else.
body.off: You can turn this off any time in Android Settings → Accessibility.

disclosure.consent: I understand and agree that Brainling uses the Accessibility service as described above.

restricted.title: Allow restricted settings first
restricted.subtitle: Android 13+ blocks Accessibility for apps installed outside Google Play. Do this once:

steps.back: Come back and turn on Accessibility

restricted.openHint: Opens Brainling's App info in Android settings

accessibility.title: Turn on Brainling in Accessibility
accessibility.path: Settings → Accessibility → Installed apps → Brainling → ON
accessibility.warning: Android will show a scary warning. That’s normal for all Accessibility apps. We only do what’s listed on the previous screen.
accessibility.banking: Some banking or payment apps ask you to pause Accessibility apps while you use them. If one asks, pause Brainling — we’ll remind you to turn it back on.
accessibility.successBody: Your Brainling can feel reels now.
